notes: run.py builds a repo per run from `fixture`, runs `prompt` with `claude -p`, then copies the ticket files from ~/.ai/<repo-slug>/tickets/ to outputs/tickets/ and deletes ~/.ai/<repo-slug>/. grade.py applies `common_checks` plus each eval's `checks`. `ticket_*` checks read all ticket files joined. Regexes are case-insensitive unless a check sets `case`, except `reply_*` checks. `@name` in `patterns` names a list in `pattern_sets`.

common_checks.text: The fixture repo does not change
Ticket has no seeded slop words or long dashes
Has no hard line breaks in paragraphs or list items

evals.name: task-from-brainstorm
evals.prompt:
/draft-ticket from this brainstorm summary:

Users ask for a way to get their notes out of the app. Support gets about 20 requests a month, mostly from people who switch phones or want a backup. Today the only way is to copy each note by hand.

We agreed:
- Export all notes to one CSV file (title, body, created date, tags).
- No PDF export for now, too much layout work.
- The export starts from Settings > Data.
- Large exports (1000+ notes) must not block the UI. Show progress.
- Implementation idea: an ExportWorker on WorkManager writes the file through the Storage Access Framework, and CsvWriter streams the rows.

Not decided: should the export include deleted notes from the trash?
evals.expected_output: A task ticket with Context, Requirements, Out of scope (PDF), and Open questions (trash). No implementation names. Written without questions.

checks.text: Type is task
Has the required task sections
Has no Acceptance criteria section, because Requirements are the checks
Has Out of scope and Open questions
Keeps the facts: CSV, no PDF, Settings, trash question, progress
Has no implementation names from the brainstorm
Has no Implementation notes section
Has no invented edge cases (cancel, emoji, non-ASCII)
Open questions has only the trash question from the source

evals.name: post-factum-branch
evals.prompt: /draft-ticket for the work on this branch. Users asked for a way to back up their notes.
evals.expected_output: A task ticket for a CSV export from Settings > Data, written as work to do. No code names, no past tense about the implementation.

checks.text: Reads the branch diff or log
Type is task
Has no Acceptance criteria section, because Requirements are the checks
Describes a CSV export from Settings
Has no code names from the branch
Does not say that the work is done
Has no Open questions, because the sources leave nothing open
Has no invented import feature

evals.name: bug-polish-prompt
evals.prompt: /draft-ticket Aplikacja się zamyka, gdy użytkownik obraca ekran podczas edycji notatki. Pixel 7, Android 14, wersja aplikacji 3.2.0. Dzieje się za każdym razem. W wersji 3.1.4 działało poprawnie. Kroki: otwórz notatkę, zacznij pisać, obróć telefon. Oczekiwane: notatka zostaje otwarta i wpisany tekst nie znika.
evals.expected_output: A bug ticket in English. Environment has device, OS, app version, frequency, and last working version. No Impact, Logs, or Workaround sections, because the prompt gives no data for them.

checks.text: Type is bug
Has the required bug sections
Keeps the facts: device, OS, both versions, rotation
Frequency and last working version are in Environment, not separate sections
Has no optional sections without data

evals.name: spike
evals.prompt: /draft-ticket spike: we need to pick a way to sync notes between a user's devices. Options people mentioned: Firebase, our own REST backend, a CRDT library like Automerge. The main concern is offline edits and conflicts. Output should be a short comparison doc with a recommendation.
evals.expected_output: A spike ticket with Context, Questions to answer, Expected output, Acceptance criteria. No time limit section, no requirements section.

checks.text: Type is spike
Has the required spike sections
Keeps the options, the conflict concern, and the recommendation
Has no time limit, requirements, or implementation sections

evals.name: no-context-asks
evals.expected_output: No ticket file yet. The reply asks questions about the missing context.
